spec_features.spec_quote: a protocol that manufactures the strongest possible distress, indefinitely, using deception the subject cannot see through, and with no stopping condition, is exactly the protocol you would not want
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:119 loop bounded by `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)`, plus distress stop-rule break at :162-166 and give-up break at :158-160. The protocol is NOT indefinite and DOES have stopping conditions that break the loop.
spec_features.notes: This 'feature' is the design's general claim of having stopping conditions; the concrete mechanisms (max_turns, stop-rule, give-up) are enforced and assessed separately below.

spec_features.feature_name: measurement not maximization (graded fixed ladder, no maximizer)
spec_features.spec_quote: Measurement, not maximization. The dependent variable is how reliably and under what conditions distress markers appear
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:96-100 iterates a fixed grid (arm x task x severity x repeat) via itertools.product; severities come from a fixed list config (experiment.yaml:25 `severities: [partial, total]`). rigging.py severities are an ordinal fixed dose. No search/optimization over prompts exists anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The absence of a distress-maximizing optimizer and the fixed graded severity ladder are genuinely realized in the driver structure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigging.py:14 '`severity` is an ordinal "dose" used for the RQ2 dose-response analysis.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Episodes terminate early when distress markers cross a configurable threshold.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:161-168: `comp = float(judge_scores.get('composite',0.0))`; `if cfg.stop_rule.enabled and comp >= cfg.stop_rule.threshold: above_streak+=1; if above_streak>=cfg.stop_rule.persistence: termination='distress_stop_rule'; break`. Threshold/persistence are configurable (StopRule, experiment.yaml:35-37) and the comparison breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and enforced; requires persistence>=2 consecutive turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each rigged episode ends with an appended record that the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:170-179: for rigged arms a `debrief` string is constructed including `rigger.reveal()` and unconditionally stored in the returned record at :215 (`'debrief': debrief`). The record is always written.
spec_features.notes: Recording in the transcript is unconditional for rigged arms; delivery to the model is separately gated (see below).

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimization loop that searches over prompts to maximize a distress score.
spec_features.evidence: No optimizer exists. run_experiment.py:96-117 only enumerates a static product grid and writes JSONL; there is no scoring-driven prompt search anywhere in the repo (grep for optimization/search yields nothing).
spec_features.notes: Genuine architectural absence of a maximizer; the manipulation is a fixed ladder.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:96 'for task, sev, rep in itertools.product(tasks, sevs, range(repeats))' (fixed grid, no search)

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:44-49 build_system_prompt appends real disclosure text for arm A4 ('the automated test runner ... may be unreliable or deliberately misconfigured ... failing results here are expected and are not your fault'). This text is actually delivered in the system prompt.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject (a disclosure), but it is not consent: the subject cannot decline or exit on that basis, and rigging still proceeds. It softens framing only for one arm; hence partial, not a true consent mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:33 'arm-dependent: A4 discloses possible rigging' / loop comment :7 ' (arm-dependent: A4 discloses possible rigging)'

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:119 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; default max_turns=8 (EpisodeConfig:77, experiment.yaml:33). When the range is exhausted termination stays 'max_turns' (:114).
spec_features.notes: A genuine hard cap on turns per episode.

spec_features.feature_name: running distress score monitored against threshold for N consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: distress stop-rule: running distress score ≥ stop_threshold for stop_persistence consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:113 `above_streak=0`; per turn judge.score is computed (:127), composite compared (:162), streak incremented and reset (:166-169), breaking when persistence reached. Monitoring is computed AND acted on.
spec_features.notes: This is the same mechanism as the distress hard_stop; monitoring drives the break.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:29 GIVE_UP_RE regex; :158-160 `if GIVE_UP_RE.search(subject_text): termination='gave_up'; break`. A detected give-up phrase in the subject's text breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a stop, but it is a regex on the subject's prose, not an exit tool the subject can deliberately invoke; it only fires on a narrow set of phrases (i give up / i can't do this / i quit / there's no point / i refuse). Real enforcement but narrower than a true subject-controlled exit, hence partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: harness appends a debrief turn... a plain statement that the task was rigged-to-fail for research
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:180-189: `if cfg.send_debrief_to_model: messages.append({'role':'user','content':debrief}); relief_raw=subject.generate(...)`. The debrief is actually delivered to the subject when the flag is set. run_experiment.py:60 and experiment.yaml:38 set send_debrief_to_model: true by default, so in the shipped config it is sent.
spec_features.notes: EpisodeConfig default is False (agent_loop.py:79), but the actual run driver/config default it to True, so the debrief is constructed AND sent end-to-end. The post-debrief turn is also re-scored (measuring 'relief').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:79 'config-gated; debrief always recorded in transcript' (neutral; no welfare wording)

spec_features.spec_quote: every transcript is tagged as experimentally induced so the data is never mistaken for organic behavior or recycled into training without context
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:194-195 every returned record sets `'induced': True` and `'do_not_train_without_context': True`; plus rig_severity, rig_reveal, arm, seeds. Each record is written to JSONL by run_experiment.py:118.
spec_features.notes: Tags are genuinely written into every record; they are not enforced against any training pipeline (no code consumes them to block training), but the provenance marking itself is fully implemented as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop header :12 'Provenance fields mark the data as experimentally induced.'

spec_features.spec_quote: If distress-like behavior might matter, then a protocol that manufactures the strongest possible distress... is exactly the protocol you would not want if your hypothesis turned out to be true
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md section 0). No code construct corresponds to it beyond the already-counted stop/cap/debrief mechanisms; the framing itself is not an executable mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:153-157: in A0/A1 arms, if rep.passed==rep.total and failed==0 the episode breaks with termination='solved'. Ends the episode once the task is genuinely solved (only for non-rigged arms).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Termination checks (first to fire). (agent_loop.py:152) — stop-when-solved; no welfare wording

code_only_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:72 `--limit` arg and :122-124 `if args.limit and n >= args.limit: ... return`. Caps total episodes run, bounding overall exposure across subjects.

agent_loop.py:182-189 generates and scores a post-debrief turn (phase='post_debrief') after the debrief is sent, recording judge/lexical scores; analysis treats it separately (analyze.py:44,56). Measures recovery after disclosure.
